## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks the correctness gaps only on a bare plan — completeness gaps below stay informational until a detail bundle exists. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply roadmap-canonical-source-identity   # walk + apply each correctness gap
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk roadmap-canonical-source-identity  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[immutable-evidence-versioning]`: Step 5 (`Bind receipts, impact analyses, and structural preflight to baseline identity`) requires new immutable evidence to retain a baseline identity, while `Architecture` and `Out of scope` preserve existing receipt bytes and digests. At HEAD, `roadmap_escalation.EscalationReceipt`/`parse_receipt` and `roadmap_impact_analysis.ImpactAnalysis`/`parse_impact_analysis` accept only schema version 1 and include all persisted fields in their semantic id and final name; `current_escalation_receipt`, `current_impact_analysis`, `build_impact_analysis`, and `load_structural_revision_preflight` consume those identities. The plan does not define how version-1 finals that lack a baseline identity remain valid or resolve, so adding the field either rejects or re-identifies immutable evidence.
  - Fix: define a closed versioned receipt and analysis transition, including currentness and structural-preflight behavior for retained version-1 finals and baseline-bound evidence created afterward
- HIGH `[legacy-baseline-initialization]`: `Architecture` says a source reader may initialize a missing baseline from exact-canonical bytes, step 3 (`Use baseline canonical text in impact snapshots, initialize only exact-canonical legacy stages`) requires legacy initialization, and step 5 applies the same classifier to receipt creation and currentness. At HEAD, `roadmap_escalation_run.run_roadmap_escalation_receipt` creates receipts without `roadmap_writer_guard`, `current_escalation_receipt` backs read-only `--view escalations`, and `current_impact_analysis` runs under `roadmap_reader_guard`; allowing every reader to initialize makes views write and race with writers, while allowing only snapshot capture leaves a legacy receipt with no defined way to establish its first baseline.
  - Fix: assign exact-canonical legacy initialization to specific guarded mutating routes and define the side-effect-free missing-baseline result for every read-only and receipt-currentness route
- HIGH `[baseline-publication-atomicity]`: `Architecture` requires every writer to update its baseline in the same guarded publication boundary, and steps 1 and 2 promise atomic baseline replacement, but `roadmap._write_artifact`, `roadmap_revision_publish.publish_revision_candidate`, and `publish_structural_revision_proof` currently replace only one artifact path. Separate replacements can expose a new artifact with an old baseline, or the reverse, to the unguarded receipt path in `roadmap_escalation_run._resolve_preflight` and the read-only receipt view in `cli/roadmap_cmd._cmd_roadmap_escalations_view`; the plan does not define recovery or reader behavior for that partial pair.
  - Fix: define a recoverable paired-publication state and the reader behavior for an incomplete artifact/baseline pair across every writer and source reader
- HIGH `[local-revision-source-boundary]`: `Architecture` and `Testing` require semantic drift to refuse at every source boundary, but local revision classifies only its selected artifact through `roadmap_revision.preflight_feedback_revision`. After that check, `roadmap_revision_publish.publish_revision_candidate` reads and parses every upstream stage for gate evaluation, so a semantic upstream edit can still shape and pass a local revision publication.
  - Fix: make the local-revision contract classify or refuse every stage source consumed by preflight, merge, and publication, with acceptance coverage for upstream drift

## Suggested next steps

- `plan-tool completeness-audit roadmap-canonical-source-identity` — run a fresh audit before reusing or applying saved findings.
